scenario.description: The CheckoutRequestValidator receives a CheckoutForm containing customer age, email address, order quantity, coupon code, and requested delivery date. Each field has an independent rule, and the API response must contain every violation, including an invalid email together with an excessive quantity and a malformed date. The validator also needs to turn independently parsed values into an OrderDraft only when all checks succeed. Rules must remain reusable for both HTTP checkout requests and batch imports, and adding a new field should not require rewriting the control flow of existing checks. A sequential pipeline that stops after the first error would be easier to implement, but it would prevent the response from showing all applicable problems. Decide how the independent checks and their results should be combined so the response semantics are explicit, failures can accumulate, and the constructed draft is produced consistently.
scenario.decision_statement: Decide how independent field checks should be combined to report every violation while avoiding accidental sequential dependencies and early termination.
scenario.notes: Applicative fits combining independent field checks with accumulated errors into one draft; monad is the near-miss (sequential short-circuiting pipeline), while contravariant-validators supports reusable cross-channel rules and functor supports mapping parsed values into the draft.
